classification.difficultyReason: Relate the line's heights across both squares using its constant slope, use the larger square's area ratio to determine that height and transfer it to the smaller square.

content.prompt: Two squares, one of side length 1, the other of side length 2, stand side by side. A straight line through the vertex of the smaller square cuts the area of the larger square in the ratio $2:1$. In what ratio does this line cut the area of the smaller square?

spec.description: Adjacent squares with aligned bases; smaller square on the left. A line runs from its bottom-left vertex through the common boundary to the larger square's right edge.
spec.mathematics: Square side lengths are 1 and 2. The line is straight; no additional heights are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Question contains only the supplied lengths and dividing line.

answer.short:
$5:1$.

Use the trapezium in the larger square to find the line's height at the common boundary.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the height of the line at the common boundary. Since the horizontal distances from the starting vertex are 1 and 3, its height at the right edge is $3x$.

The lower region in the larger square is a trapezium:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{lower, large}}&=\frac{(x+3x)\times2}{2}\\A_{\text{lower, large}}&=4x.\end{align*}$$
The diagram shows the upper region is larger, so
$$\begin{align*}4-4x&=2(4x)\\4&=12x\\x&=\frac13.\end{align*}$$
In the smaller square,
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{lower, small}}&=\frac{1\times\frac13}{2}\\A_{\text{lower, small}}&=\frac16,\\A_{\text{upper, small}}&=1-\frac16\\A_{\text{upper, small}}&=\frac56.\end{align*}$$
Thus the upper-to-lower area ratio is $\frac56:\frac16=5:1$.
